He writes Ted about Rabelais and other writers, Quentin learning baseball from the butler James, and Archie losing his head and steering into the other boat at Groton.

headline: The Governors' Conference opens
summary: The Governors' Conference on conserving the nation's resources opens in the East Room, and Roosevelt sits in from 10:30 to 2:30 before turning to appointments. Archie Butt attends his first White House luncheon, with Yale's President Hadley, the Cowleses and the Lodges. Roosevelt asks Speaker Cannon to pass a bill making the Inland Waterways Commission permanent; it fails.

headline: Second day with the governors
summary: Roosevelt again spends 10:30 to 2:30 at the conservation conference, then discusses the anti-injunction bill and a Norfolk Navy Yard contract. After tennis with Winthrop, Cooley and Meyer, he thanks the Kaiser for a letter and gift and tells him about the fleet. Edith goes to the National Theater.

headline: Governors declare for conservation
summary: The Governors' Conference closes with a declaration in favor of conservation; 38 states go on to form conservation commissions, and the meeting gives rise to the annual governors' conferences. Pinchot will call it the first national gathering anywhere to treat resource protection as a single problem. Roosevelt creates Kansas National Forest, lunches with historian James Ford Rhodes, and holds a reception; rain turns the planned garden party into a White House tea.

headline: Peary's next Arctic push
summary: Roosevelt discusses the Rainy River dam bill, sees John Mitchell, Borah and others, and talks with Robert Peary about his coming Arctic expedition. He speaks at the Methodist gathering at American University near Tenleytown, opens a St. Louis charity bazaar by pressing a button, and plays tennis.

headline: Roswell gets kicked
summary: Archie Butt is called to the White House because Roosevelt's horse Roswell has been kicked, and finds the President calmer than he expected. Timothy Woodruff comes in the evening to talk New York politics. Roosevelt tells Archie that Quentin is wrapped up in baseball and the grounds are in full bloom.

headline: Checking on the fleet's progress
summary: Roosevelt discusses Kentucky patronage, plays tennis, dines with the Cowleses and the Italian ambassador, and meets Taft late on canal business. He writes Captain Cone of the torpedo flotilla traveling with the fleet about what the cruise has done so far.

headline: Election fraud in Panama
summary: The Cabinet discusses election fraud in Panama. Roosevelt meets congressmen on the Inland Waterways bill, sees Newberry and Pinchot, and dines with Metcalf. Miss Potter and Mr. and Mrs. Harvier are house guests.

headline: Ship subsidies and the Sherman Act
summary: Roosevelt meets Speaker Cannon at ten, then discusses anti-injunction legislation, Sherman Act amendments and the ship subsidy in the postal bill. After tennis with Garfield and Jusserand he dines with Bacon. David Gray and Miss Potter are staying.

headline: Clarence Darrow calls late
summary: Roosevelt discusses Venezuela with Cullom and the Rainy River dam with Bede, Hepburn, Garfield and Stevens, and hears a delegation pushing battleship work at the Norfolk yard. He lunches with Root, General Young and his wife, and others, rides, and at ten that night receives Clarence Darrow and Lincoln Steffens.

headline: Admiral Evans calls
summary: After the Cabinet meeting, Admiral Robley Evans, Senator Sutherland and Representative Langley call. Roosevelt discusses New York politics with Wadsworth, plays tennis, and writes Albert Shaw about the coming convention.

headline: A range for the bison; the little bear leaves
summary: A new law creates the National Bison Range in Montana, starting with 18,000 acres and 80 bison, and Roosevelt declares the Minnesota National Forest. He writes Edward Buxton about planning next year's African trip, and tells Ted, who is deciding what to do in the fall, that it pains him to see "the little bear" heading out into the world.

headline: Envoys from Liberia
summary: Roosevelt meets Senators Beveridge and Kean, grants Austrian Ambassador Hengelmüller a private audience, and with Root receives three envoys from Liberia. After tennis he discusses Indian Territory with Garfield. He tells Whitelaw Reid he dislikes the custom of presentation at court. Archie Butt escorts Edith to the theater.

headline: A noon wedding on N Street
summary: Roosevelt goes to a noon wedding at 1753 N Street, where Francis R. Stevens marries Elizabeth Oliver. Between conferences with his cabinet, he talks with Depew about the government liability bill and with Fassett about James S. Sherman for Vice President, lunches with Colonel Hugh Scott, and rides.

headline: Spanish War veterans and Taft
summary: Senator Bourne calls in the morning and Walter Hale, representing veterans of the war with Spain, at 11:30. Roosevelt confers with Taft and Root in the afternoon and plays tennis at 4:30.

headline: The New Haven merger will stand
summary: Father Doyle brings twelve student priests to call, along with the District commissioners, and Roosevelt rides at five. He writes Alston Dayton about West Virginia delegates for Taft, John Hull on revising Army promotions, and Lodge that the New Haven railroad combination will not be broken up.

headline: Seven sets and mint juleps
summary: Roosevelt plays seven sets of tennis with Archie Butt, Garfield and Captain McCoy, after which they all have mint juleps, joined by the Longworths, Pinchot and others. He gives Fitzhugh Lee a pistol. He tells Alston Dayton he will not let his name go on the ballot, and Lyman Abbott that he will not be renominated.

headline: Congress adjourns; Quentin's beehive
summary: The Aldrich-Vreeland currency bill passes and Congress adjourns; Roosevelt signs the last bills at the Capitol that evening. He rides with Archie Butt, lunches with Ranger Bill McDonald and Admiral Cowles, and plays tennis. To Kermit he describes summery evenings under the apple tree with Edith and La Follette's filibuster; to Archie, Quentin's new beehive and a foul tip to the eye.

headline: Ted graduates from Harvard
summary: Roosevelt calls on J. J. Gaff at 1520 20th Street to see a painting of a farmer, and dines with the Jusserands. "The Successful Mother" by Roosevelt appears in the Ladies' Home Journal, and Ted finishes at Harvard. Archie Butt has become Edith's regular escort on solo outings, long walks and antique hunts. On June 18 the Republicans will nominate Taft.
